concept.principles.title: The Framework for Trust by Design
concept.principles.subtitle: Five principles that transform compliance into competitive advantage.
concept.principles.principle1Desc: Users maintain meaningful control over AI decisions affecting them. Systems suggest rather than impose, explain rather than dictate, and always provide clear paths to human oversight.
concept.principles.principle2Desc: Inclusive design isn't an add-on — it's the baseline. Every interface, algorithm, and interaction pattern must serve the full spectrum of human cognitive and physical abilities from inception.
concept.principles.principle3Desc: Technology should never make users feel inadequate. Error messages become learning opportunities. Security measures respect context. Failures are system problems, never user deficiencies.
concept.principles.principle4Desc: Trust isn't built through obscurity but through clarity. Users should understand what data is collected, how algorithms make decisions, and why certain actions are required — without needing technical expertise.
concept.principles.principle5Desc: Perfect prevention is impossible; graceful recovery is essential. Design clear pathways for users to resolve issues, appeal decisions, and regain access with minimal friction and maximum dignity.

findings.title: Research Findings
findings.subtitle: Evidence-based insights from community contributions, driving policy change and better design
findings.pub1Desc: Analysis of 89 reports documenting how SMS-based authentication creates insurmountable barriers for seniors without smartphones or in areas with poor cellular coverage.
findings.pub2Desc: 78 documented cases where account lockout policies provided no recovery mechanism for seniors who forgot complex passwords.
findings.pub3Desc: Examination of 64 reports showing how complex password requirements force seniors to write down credentials, creating different security risks.
findings.pub3Finding2: Avg 8 character requirements exceeded memory capacity
findings.quarterlyDesc: Regular summaries of emerging patterns from community submissions, shared with contributors first
findings.q2Point1: New pattern: Biometric authentication confusion increasing
findings.q2Point2: Healthcare portals show highest friction (67 reports)
findings.q2Point3: Knowledge Gap remains dominant harm type (45%)
findings.q1Point3: First policy change implemented in UK healthcare system
findings.policyDesc: Where this research has informed real-world policy changes
findings.policy1Desc: NHS Digital updated their security guidelines to require alternative authentication methods for patients who cannot use SMS-based 2FA.
findings.policy1Evidence: Evidence Used: Research report on SMS barriers, 34 UK-specific case studies
findings.policy2Desc: EU Commission launched accessibility review of electronic identification systems, citing Trust by Design evidence.
findings.policy2Evidence: Evidence Used: Aggregate data on identity verification failures
findings.emerging1Desc: Analysis of 23 recent reports documenting confusion and failures with facial recognition and fingerprint systems.
findings.emerging2Desc: Examining how seniors rely on family members to overcome security barriers, and the dignity implications.

ethics.title: Research Ethics & Data Handling
ethics.subtitle: Transparency about how we collect, protect, and use your contributions
ethics.commitment1: All stories are anonymized before analysis or publication
ethics.commitment2: You can withdraw your data at any time
ethics.commitment3: We will never sell or share your contact information
ethics.commitment4: Research findings will be publicly accessible
ethics.anonymizationIntro: Before any story is included in research analysis or publications, we:
ethics.anonymizationStep1: Remove all identifying information including names, addresses, specific dates, and unique details that could identify individuals
ethics.anonymizationStep2: Generalize locations to country or region level (never specific cities or municipalities)
ethics.anonymizationStep3: Replace proper nouns with generic terms (e.g., "a healthcare portal" instead of specific service names)
ethics.anonymizationStep4: Aggregate age ranges and demographic information to prevent re-identification
ethics.contactInfoDesc: If you provide an email address for follow-up, it is stored separately from your story and encrypted. It is never included in any published data or shared with third parties.
ethics.objectivesIntro: This research aims to document and analyze patterns in how security measures create barriers to government digital services for senior citizens and other vulnerable populations. Our goals are to:
ethics.withdrawDesc: You can withdraw your submission at any time before publication. Contact us with your submission ID, and we will remove your story from the dataset. Note: Once data appears in a published report, we cannot remove it from that publication, but will exclude it from future analysis.
ethics.correctionDesc: If you notice an error in your submission or want to add important details, contact us with your submission ID. We will update your entry in our database.
ethics.accessRightDesc: You can request a copy of your original submission and see how it has been categorized in our analysis system. Contact us with your submission ID.
ethics.reviewDesc: This research has been reviewed and approved by an independent ethics committee to ensure it meets standards for ethical research involving human participants.
